source_user: Advanced cluster case Mooncake-35: Analyze Mooncake-style disaggregated KV-cache or serving architecture for a long-context workload. Variant 35 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: define prefill/decode ownership, KV placement and eviction, RDMA transfer cost, cache consistency, admission control, failure recovery, and comparison against local or conventional distributed serving. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Treat Mooncake-style KV disaggregation for variant 35 as a hypothesis, not an assumed optimization. Assume a long-context multi-node service, but first record model/runtime versions, GPU and NIC types, PCIe/NUMA topology, link capacity, memory budgets, failure domains, prompt/output distributions, and concurrency; mark unknowns explicitly. Assign prefill workers prompt computation and decode workers token generation, and specify KV block layout and precision, ownership, placement, replication, eviction/TTL, version/checksum validation, batching, admission limits, migration, and handling of stale or partial blocks.

Falsifiable hypothesis: under a pre-registered offered load and workload mix, remote KV placement improves throughput or p99 inter-token latency by a stated margin versus a colocated/local-KV and conventional distributed-serving baseline, without violating TTFT, error-rate, freshness, memory, or recovery SLOs. Keep model, sampling, warm-up, cache state, batching, concurrency, and admission policy matched. Measure TTFT, time-to-first-byte, inter-token and end-to-end latency (ms), tokens/s, cache hit/miss and reuse, bytes transferred, RDMA bandwidth/latency, queue depth, GPU/NIC utilization, memory/evictions, correctness, and error rates with synchronized timestamps, p50/p95/p99, repetitions, and confidence intervals. Attribute gains separately from prefill, decode, KV lookup, serialization, RDMA, queueing, and cache warmup; report topology and units.

Test cache consistency with versioned blocks, concurrent updates, retries, duplicate requests, and checksum or model-layer validation. Exercise cache-node loss, stale/partial transfer, RDMA/link loss, decode/prefill worker loss, and control-plane failure. Use bounded retries, admission backpressure, replica or recomputation fallback, request isolation and authorization; do not expose another tenant's KV. Disable the feature on corruption, freshness violation, error/SLO regression, memory pressure, or a pre-registered rollback threshold, then use the conventional path and preserve diagnostics. Evidence is required before claiming improvement: read-only inventory, matched baseline, raw telemetry, repeated controlled trials, and authorized fault-injection/correctness results. Do not infer production benefit from synthetic data or unverified platform semantics.

source_user: Advanced cluster case Mooncake-44: Analyze Mooncake-style disaggregated KV-cache or serving architecture for a long-context workload. Variant 44 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: define prefill/decode ownership, KV placement and eviction, RDMA transfer cost, cache consistency, admission control, failure recovery, and comparison against local or conventional distributed serving. corrected_answer:
Treat Mooncake-style KV disaggregation for variant 44 as a hypothesis, not an assumed optimization. Assume a long-context multi-node service, but first record model/runtime versions, GPU and NIC types, PCIe/NUMA topology, link capacity, memory budgets, failure domains, prompt/output distributions, and concurrency; mark unknowns explicitly. Assign prefill workers prompt computation and decode workers token generation, and specify KV block layout and precision, ownership, placement, replication, eviction/TTL, version/checksum validation, batching, admission limits, migration, and handling of stale or partial blocks.

Falsifiable hypothesis: under a pre-registered offered load and workload mix, remote KV placement improves throughput or p99 inter-token latency by a stated margin versus a colocated/local-KV and conventional distributed-serving baseline, without violating TTFT, error-rate, freshness, memory, or recovery SLOs. Keep model, sampling, warm-up, cache state, batching, concurrency, and admission policy matched. Measure TTFT, time-to-first-byte, inter-token and end-to-end latency (ms), tokens/s, cache hit/miss and reuse, bytes transferred, RDMA bandwidth/latency, queue depth, GPU/NIC utilization, memory/evictions, correctness, and error rates with synchronized timestamps, p50/p95/p99, repetitions, and confidence intervals. Attribute gains separately from prefill, decode, KV lookup, serialization, RDMA, queueing, and cache warmup; report topology and units.

Test cache consistency with versioned blocks, concurrent updates, retries, duplicate requests, and checksum or model-layer validation. Exercise cache-node loss, stale/partial transfer, RDMA/link loss, decode/prefill worker loss, and control-plane failure. Use bounded retries, admission backpressure, replica or recomputation fallback, request isolation and authorization; do not expose another tenant's KV. Disable the feature on corruption, freshness violation, error/SLO regression, memory pressure, or a pre-registered rollback threshold, then use the conventional path and preserve diagnostics. Evidence is required before claiming improvement: read-only inventory, matched baseline, raw telemetry, repeated controlled trials, and authorized fault-injection/correctness results. Do not infer production benefit from synthetic data or unverified platform semantics.
